ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The upper figure (i) in the figure is a single-line diagram; on the left side is an alternator, connected to the bus labeled 2, then connected through transformer T1 to the bus labeled 1, and on the right side connected to a synchronous motor. In the positive-sequence network of figure (ii), bus 2 is on the left and bus 1 is on the right; on the generator side there is a source Eg'' in series with j0.1 to bus 2, between bus 2 and bus 1 is j0.1, and between bus 1 and the motor-side source Em'' is j0.3. The negative-sequence network of figure (iii) has the same structure but no sources, containing j0.1, j0.1, and j0.3. Figure (iv) gives the zero-sequence network, but a line-to-line fault does not need the zero-sequence network. Reasoning: The fault point is at bus 1, is a b-c two-phase bolted line-to-line fault, and the pre-fault current is neglected. According to a two-phase short-circuit fault, the zero-sequence current I0 = 0, so only the positive-sequence and negative-sequence equivalent impedances are needed. Short-circuit the sources in the positive-sequence network; looking into the system from bus 1, the left-side path is j0.1 from bus 1 to bus 2 plus the generator-side j0.1, namely j0.2; the right-side motor branch is j0.3. Therefore Z1_th = j0.3 || j0.2 = j(0.3 || 0.2) = j(0.3×0.2/(0.3+0.2)) = j0.12. From the figure, the negative-sequence network has the same impedance, so Z2_th = j0.12. For a line-to-line fault, the magnitude of the positive-sequence current |I1| = |1/(Z1_th + Z2_th)| = |1/(j0.24)| = 4.1667 p.u. The problem asks for the magnitude of the line-to-line fault current from phase b to phase c, |If| = sqrt(3)|I1| = 1.732×4.1667 = 7.2169 p.u., rounded to 7.22 p.u.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the sequence diagrams show bus 1 on the right, bus 2 on the left, with positive and negative sequence reactances j0.1 from generator to bus 2, j0.1 between buses, and j0.3 from bus 1 to the synchronous motor. Then reason as follows: looking into bus 1 in the positive-sequence network with sources shorted gives Z1_th = j0.3 || j(0.1+0.1) = j0.12. From the negative-sequence diagram, Z2_th is identical: Z2_th = j0.12. For an LL fault, ignore the zero-sequence network and compute I1 = 1/(Z1_th + Z2_th) = 1/(j0.24). The requested current from phase b to c has magnitude sqrt(3)|I1|, which evaluates to about 7.22 p.u.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the bus-1 fault location and the two paths from bus 1 in the positive/negative sequence diagrams: a j0.3 motor path and a j0.2 alternator-side path made of j0.1 plus j0.1. Let the common sequence voltage at the fault be V, since a bolted b-c fault gives V1 = V2. Positive-sequence current supplied into the fault is (1 - V)/j0.2 + (1 - V)/j0.3. Negative-sequence current absorbed by the passive negative network is V/j0.2 + V/j0.3. Enforce the LL-fault condition I1 = -I2, equivalently positive current supplied equals negative-network current, giving V = 0.5 because the positive and negative admittance sums are identical. Then |I1| = |(1 - 0.5)(1/j0.2 + 1/j0.3)| = 4.1667 p.u. Convert sequence current to the actual b-c line current magnitude using |I_bc| = sqrt(3)|I1|, giving 7.22 p.u.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中 figure (i) 是两母线系统，母线 2 侧为 alternator，经标为 T1 的 Y-Δ 变压器连接到母线 1 侧的 synchronous motor；故障位置在题述母线 1 的 b-c 相间短路处。figure (ii) 正序网络中，从母线 1 看出去有两条通路：一条到同步电动机支路，电抗为 j0.3；另一条经线路/变压器 j0.1 到母线 2，再经发电机支路 j0.1，因此 alternator 侧等效为 j0.2。figure (iii) 负序网络也显示同样的两条从母线 1 出发的无源电抗通路：j0.3 电动机支路和 j0.1+j0.1=j0.2 发电机侧支路。figure (iv) 为零序网络，但 b-c 相间故障不涉及零序电流。推理：对 bolted line-to-line fault，I0=0，且故障点正序、负序电压满足 V1=V2=V，正负序电流满足 I1=-I2。忽略故障前电流，正序等效源取 1 p.u.，正序向故障点供给的电流为 (1−V)/j0.2 + (1−V)/j0.3。负序网络吸收的电流为 V/j0.2 + V/j0.3。由 I1=-I2，即正序供给电流等于负序网络电流，得 (1−V)(1/j0.2+1/j0.3)=V(1/j0.2+1/j0.3)，所以 V=0.5。于是 |I1|=|(1−0.5)(1/j0.2+1/j0.3)|=0.5(5+3.3333)=4.1667 p.u.。b-c 相间故障的实际线间故障电流幅值为 |Ibc|=√3|I1|=√3×4.1667=7.2169 p.u.，四舍五入为 7.22 p.u.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For a b-c bolted line-to-line fault, the sequence boundary conditions are I0 = 0, V1 = V2 at the fault point, and I1 = -I2. With neglected prefault currents, both positive-sequence internal emfs may be represented as 1 p.u. behind their positive-sequence reactance paths.

solver_metadata.cot_raw: 图像描述：图中 figure (i) 是两母线系统，母线 2 侧为 alternator，经标为 T1 的 Y-Δ 变压器连接到母线 1 侧的 synchronous motor；故障位置在题述母线 1 的 b-c 相间短路处。figure (ii) 正序网络中，从母线 1 看出去有两条通路：一条到同步电动机支路，电抗为 j0.3；另一条经线路/变压器 j0.1 到母线 2，再经发电机支路 j0.1，因此 alternator 侧等效为 j0.2。figure (iii) 负序网络也显示同样的两条从母线 1 出发的无源电抗通路：j0.3 电动机支路和 j0.1+j0.1=j0.2 发电机侧支路。figure (iv) 为零序网络，但 b-c 相间故障不涉及零序电流。推理：对 bolted line-to-line fault，I0=0，且故障点正序、负序电压满足 V1=V2=V，正负序电流满足 I1=-I2。忽略故障前电流，正序等效源取 1 p.u.，正序向故障点供给的电流为 (1−V)/j0.2 + (1−V)/j0.3。负序网络吸收的电流为 V/j0.2 + V/j0.3。由 I1=-I2，即正序供给电流等于负序网络电流，得 (1−V)(1/j0.2+1/j0.3)=V(1/j0.2+1/j0.3)，所以 V=0.5。于是 |I1|=|(1−0.5)(1/j0.2+1/j0.3)|=0.5(5+3.3333)=4.1667 p.u.。b-c 相间故障的实际线间故障电流幅值为 |Ibc|=√3|I1|=√3×4.1667=7.2169 p.u.，四舍五入为 7.22 p.u.

raw_record.original_question: The two-bus power system shown in figure (i) has one alternator supplying a synchronous motor load through a (Y - Δ) transformer. The positive-, negative-, and zero-sequence diagrams of the system are shown in figures (ii), (iii), and (iv), respectively. All reactances in the sequence diagrams are in p.u. For a bolted line-to-line fault (fault impedance = zero) between phases 'b' and 'c' at bus 1, neglecting all pre-fault currents, the magnitude of the fault current (from phase 'b' to 'c') in p.u. is ______ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The upper figure (i) in the figure is a single-line diagram; on the left side is an alternator, connected to the bus labeled 2, then connected through transformer T1 to the bus labeled 1, and on the right side connected to a synchronous motor. In the positive-sequence network of figure (ii), bus 2 is on the left and bus 1 is on the right; on the generator side there is a source Eg'' in series with j0.1 to bus 2, between bus 2 and bus 1 is j0.1, and between bus 1 and the motor-side source Em'' is j0.3. The negative-sequence network of figure (iii) has the same structure but no sources, containing j0.1, j0.1, and j0.3. Figure (iv) gives the zero-sequence network, but a line-to-line fault does not need the zero-sequence network.
Reasoning: The fault point is at bus 1, is a b-c two-phase bolted line-to-line fault, and the pre-fault current is neglected. According to a two-phase short-circuit fault, the zero-sequence current I0 = 0, so only the positive-sequence and negative-sequence equivalent impedances are needed. Short-circuit the sources in the positive-sequence network; looking into the system from bus 1, the left-side path is j0.1 from bus 1 to bus 2 plus the generator-side j0.1, namely j0.2; the right-side motor branch is j0.3. Therefore Z1_th = j0.3 || j0.2 = j(0.3 || 0.2) = j(0.3×0.2/(0.3+0.2)) = j0.12. From the figure, the negative-sequence network has the same impedance, so Z2_th = j0.12. For a line-to-line fault, the magnitude of the positive-sequence current |I1| = |1/(Z1_th + Z2_th)| = |1/(j0.24)| = 4.1667 p.u. The problem asks for the magnitude of the line-to-line fault current from phase b to phase c, |If| = sqrt(3)|I1| = 1.732×4.1667 = 7.2169 p.u., rounded to 7.22 p.u.
